title: Chemical spill in the lab
summary: A bottle of acid breaks on the bench and splashes a classmate. Act fast and safely.
sources: CLEAPSS Student Safety Sheets and school laboratory guidance
Standard school lab first-aid practice: rinse skin with running water

scenes.narration: Crash! A bottle of dilute sulfuric acid slips off the shelf. Acid spreads over the bench and drips onto the floor. Your lab partner shouts that some splashed on her hand.

choices.label: It's a spill and someone is hurt: tell the teacher now
choices.feedback: Yes. A spill with a casualty: the teacher must know straight away.

choices.label: It's only dilute. Keep working.
choices.feedback: Even dilute acid irritates skin and eyes, and a spill can spread. It needs dealing with now.

scenes.narration: The teacher is coming. Your partner's hand is stinging and red. Other students are crowding round.

choices.label: Help her rinse her hand under cold running water, and keep rinsing
choices.feedback: Right. Rinse chemical splashes with lots of running water for at least 10 to 20 minutes.

choices.label: Wipe her hand with a paper towel
choices.feedback: Wiping can spread the acid. Running water washes it away.

choices.label: Put some sodium hydroxide on it to neutralise it
choices.feedback: Never put another chemical on skin. Alkali burns too, and the reaction releases heat. Use water only.

scenes.narration: Acid is still dripping from the bench. Students are stepping close to look.

choices.label: Ask everyone to step back and keep away from the spill
choices.feedback: Yes. Keep people away so no one steps in it or gets splashed. Your teacher will deal with the spill.

choices.label: Mop it up with paper towels in your bare hands
choices.feedback: Never handle a chemical spill with bare hands. The teacher uses a spill kit and protective gloves.

choices.label: Pick up the broken glass pieces
choices.feedback: Broken glass covered in acid can cut and burn you. Leave it for the teacher with the right equipment.

scenes.narration: The teacher arrives with the spill kit. Your partner is still rinsing her hand.

choices.label: Tell the teacher what spilled, how much, and who was splashed
choices.feedback: Good. Clear information helps the teacher treat the casualty and clean up correctly.

choices.label: Go back to your own experiment
choices.feedback: Stay and help: the teacher needs to know exactly what happened.

end-safe.text: The teacher neutralises and clears the spill with the kit. Your partner's hand calms down after rinsing, and she is checked by the school nurse.

end-unsafe.text: The spill spread and more people were splashed.

learn: Tell the teacher immediately about any spill or splash.
Rinse chemical splashes on skin with lots of running water; never use another chemical.
Keep everyone away from the spill and broken glass.
Only the teacher clears spills, using a spill kit and protective gloves.
disclaimer: Training only. This is not a substitute for emergency services or certified first-aid and fire-safety training. In a real emergency in India, call 112.
